title: Cross-SDK behavior PRD: deterministic pagination, idempotent retries, and resilient streaming
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: This PRD defines cross-language SDK behavior for three related client features used by Redwood customers: pagination, retry semantics, and streaming responses. Goal is a deterministic, testable contract for Python, TypeScript, and Go clients that preserves backward compatibility for major SDK users and eliminates common gotchas (duplicate items, stuck cursors, non-idempotent retries, and partial stream state loss).

Problems observed: duplicate results under concurrent pagination; divergent cursor formats across SDKs; ambiguous retry behavior leading to double-charges or duplicated side-effects; streaming reconnection behavior not standardized (clients either restart stream or raise errors, leading to inconsistent UX); lack of guidance on compatibility policy when we change token formats or add new streaming events.

Goals:
- Define a single pagination contract (opaque cursor token with clear semantics) supported consistently across SDKs.
- Standardize idempotency and retry policy for all mutating and non-mutating RPCs (idempotency key handling, retryable errors, backoff policy).
- Define streaming protocol (event framing, resume tokens, reconnect semantics, partial-message behavior) so SDKs can provide consistent APIs and helpers.
- Provide migration guidance and feature flags for rolling changes that affect tokens or wire format.

Non-goals:
- This PRD does not mandate server-side implementation details beyond token semantics and error classes.
- Not addressing end-to-end transactional guarantees for multi-request workflows (separate initiative).

Cross-SDK contracts (high level):
1) Pagination:
- Server returns items and an opaque string cursor token "next_cursor" when more results exist. Token semantics: referentially opaque to clients; token must encode server-side resume point but may be rotated by server releases.
- Two pagination modes: cursor-based (preferred) and offset-based (legacy for small endpoints). New endpoints must support cursor-based.
- Clients must expose both an iterator-style API and a page-level API. Iterator must hide network calls and surface stable ordering semantics.
- Clients must expose a helper to persist and later resume using the opaque cursor token unchanged.
- If server invalidates a token, it returns 410 GONE with structured error code "cursor_invalid". SDKs must surface this as CursorInvalidError with a recommended fallback to restarting enumeration from the beginning.

2) Retries and idempotency: 
- All SDKs must accept an optional idempotency_key parameter for mutating calls. If provided, SDKs attach this as Idempotency-Key header.
- Retryable errors: network failures (timeout, connection reset), 429 (rate limit), 503 (temporarily unavailable). Non-retryable: 400, 401, 403, 404, 409 unless explicitly documented.
- Retry policy: default max_attempts=4, initial_backoff=200ms, multiplier=2.0, max_backoff=8s, jitter=full jitter per AWS best practices.
- Clients must expose a retry policy config object for override and expose hooks to observe retry attempts for telemetry.
- SDK must not automatically retry if request has streaming body or custom non-idempotent side effects unless idempotency_key is present.

3) Streaming APIs:
- Streams are modeled as an event sequence over a single HTTP/2 or WebSocket connection. Server frames three top-level event types: data, progress, and end. Each data event may include an optional resume_token.
- Resume tokens are optional per event. If provided, they can be used to resume the stream after a reconnect without re-applying already-delivered events. If resume_token is missing, client should assume ordering but cannot easily dedupe after reconnect.
- SDKs must implement automatic reconnect with exponential backoff up to 5 attempts, and must attempt resume when a resume_token was last seen and server supports resume.
- If resume fails (server rejects token), the SDK surfaces a StreamResumptionFailedError and provides the user control to either restart or surface the partial state.
- Streaming API surface: Python async iterator; TS AsyncIterable<Event>; Go channel-based receiver with context for cancellation. Each SDK should provide a helper that converts streaming into a resumable checkpointable iterator (save last resume_token).

Compatibility and rollout:
- Server may change internal cursor encoding; to avoid breaking clients, server supports versioned cursors with an upstream prefix like "v1:" or "v2:". When server introduces incompatible cursor changes, it will emit a new cursor prefix and add a deprecation header for 90 days.
- SDK policy: accept any opaque cursor and surface raw token to consumers. If cursor prefix unknown and server returns 410 with code "cursor_unrecognized", SDK surfaces CursorVersionMismatch with guidance link.
- Wire changes for streaming event types are additive only; new event types must be ignored gracefully by older SDKs with an UnknownEvent type.

Telemetry and observability requirements:
- SDKs must emit metrics/events for: pagination token invalidation count, retry attempts (per error class), streaming resumption attempts and successes/failures, and idempotency key usage rate. These must be hookable to Redwood Console.

Testing and acceptance: see acceptance_criteria.

Rollout plan: server-side gate first for new cursor format behind feature-flag per customer. Publish SDK patch that tolerates both formats and exposes CursorVersionMismatch. After 90 days of opt-in telemetry, flip default to new format and bump server default.
acceptance_criteria: Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs expose iterator-style and page-style pagination APIs that return 'next_cursor' exactly as received from server and can resume using it without client transformation.
SDKs return CursorInvalidError when server responds 410 cursor_invalid and provide a clear migration recommendation in error message.
Mutating SDK calls accept an optional idempotency_key and will attach header correctly; retries follow default policy and are overrideable by consumer config.
SDKs do not auto-retry non-idempotent requests unless an idempotency_key is supplied.
Streaming SDKs implement automatic reconnect with resume attempt when a resume_token was last seen; they surface StreamResumptionFailedError when resume rejected.
All SDKs surface UnknownEvent for unrecognized streaming event types without crashing.
SDKs emit telemetry hooks for pagination invalidations, retry metrics, streaming resumption attempts, and idempotency key usage.

End-to-end integration tests for each SDK validating: normal pagination completion, token invalidation handling, retry backoff behavior, stream reconnect and resume with resume_token, and resume failure path are present in CI.
Documentation pages for each SDK (Python/TS/Go) with code samples for pagination iteration, idempotency_key usage, and stream resume are published and linked from the release notes.
comments: 2026-03-01 Aisha Patel: Drafted initial PRD after reviewing incidents: INC-2026-11 (pagination duplication) and INC-2026-08 (stream disconnects). Added high-level contracts and goals.

2026-03-03 Marcus Liu (Engineering): Requested concrete error codes for cursor invalidation and cursor_unrecognized. Suggested 410 with structured error.code for machine handling. Also requested explicit retryable error list which is included in this revision.

2026-03-05 Priya Verma (Design): Requested clearer UX guidance for resume failures in the Console and sample user-facing messages; added recommended text for CursorVersionMismatch and StreamResumptionFailedError.
2026-03-07 SRE review (eng-sre): Asked for telemetry emit points and suggested using existing tracing span conventions for retries and stream resumption; added to telemetry requirements.

2026-03-10 Marcus Liu: Engineering initial implementation plan: common spec parser to normalize cursor tokens across SDKs, shared retry logic library for all SDKs, and streaming helper modules. Blocker: need server to return resume_token consistently for long-lived streams (ENG-3012).

2026-03-12 QA: Added test matrix items for CI: pagination happy path, invalid cursor handling, retry classification coverage, streaming resume with and without resume_token, and behavior when UnknownEvent arrives.

2026-03-14 Aisha Patel: PRD updated with compatibility/rollout guidance and release timing. Marking as Planned and assigning to Marcus Liu for implementation scoping. Next: engineering to produce RFC and initial API surface PRs for each SDK repository.
